clue.text: We tore accusers to shreds with relish

indicators.note: tearing something to shreds breaks it up, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone tears their accusers apart, and enjoys doing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with relish' reads as 'gleefully', but 'relish' is the definition, a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: This spicy brown sauce is a classic condiment, and a relish is any tangy accompaniment to food.

clue.text: Short of vitality, in summary

definitions.meaning: a briefing or quick overview of facts

explanation.definitionFit: Feeling exhausted is one sense, and an outline briefing of the main points the other.

clue.text: The impetuosity one finds in Ireland

indicators.note: says the letters are found sitting inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: Ireland is where you meet dash and passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash and flair: spirited impetus or verve.

clue.text: Superb spinning toy given to Nick

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins
a nick is a small cut or notch

explanation.surface: A child named Nick receives a wonderful spinning toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a boy's name; it means a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: First-rate and excellent are synonyms.

clue.text: I'd ring around when travelling

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says they will phone round while on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on horseback or in a vehicle is a way of journeying.

clue.text: Sam's abroad, working as representative

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are worked over into another order

explanation.surface: Sam is overseas, employed as an agent.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy represents his or her country abroad.

clue.text: Most near to being defeated in court

indicators.note: in places the losing word inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: loses means is defeated

explanation.surface: A litigant is on the brink of losing a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearest is the superlative of near, as is this word of close.

clue.text: Eccentric French writer completes various small articles

parts.note: odd means eccentric
George Sand was a French novelist
ends means finishes off

explanation.surface: A quirky French author finishes a run of short pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' suggests writing; here it means items.
explanation.definitionFit: Bits and pieces: miscellaneous leftover items.

clue.text: Not bettered, but not given Test place

definitions.meaning: never topped or exceeded, as a record that stays unbeaten
never awarded a cap by being picked for a national Test match side

explanation.surface: A player whose record was never beaten, yet was never chosen for the national team.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'cap' is awarded in Britain for playing for one's country; a Test is an international match, as in cricket or rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: To cap a performance is to outdo it, and a player capped is one picked for the national side.

clue.text: Fair, to put money into security

indicators.note: into says one piece is placed inside the word for security

parts.note: a bond is a security, a certificate of debt sold to investors
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An investor is told it is reasonable to put cash into bonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair hair is light-coloured, the same pale shade as blond.

clue.text: Each April, go for a trip to the islands

indicators.note: a trip suggests the letters stumble and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: An annual April holiday to the islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' reads as a journey; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain or group of islands, as in the Greek Aegean.

clue.text: About to tie up some space

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for tying up is read backwards

parts.note: to moor a boat is to tie it up

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of tying up a boat in a little space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'About' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A room is an amount of space, as in having room to move.

clue.text: Children Tyson urges to fight

indicators.note: fighting suggests a scrap, so these letters are thrown about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Boxer Mike Tyson spurs on kids to start brawling.
explanation.definitionFit: Young people or kids are synonyms for children.

clue.text: In a highly sticky position?

parts.note: an idiom for being in trouble, read literally as being high up in a tree that oozes gum

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stuck in a difficult predicament.

clue.text: Personally select worker and tool

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as a farmhand
a pick is a digging tool

explanation.surface: Someone chooses their own labourer and equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: To choose things oneself, one at a time, is a careful personal selection.

clue.text: Be quick to punish in absence of head

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for punishing goes missing, as if beheaded

parts.note: to chasten is to punish or discipline

explanation.surface: Discipline should be swift when the head teacher is away.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurry is to move fast or be speedy.

clue.text: Wrong-headed, to use half the period on poetry

indicators.note: half keeps the first three of the six letters of period

parts.note: verse means poetry

explanation.surface: It is foolish to spend half of a lesson on poems.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrary and stubbornly unreasonable are close synonyms.

clue.text: For breather during exercise, jump into pool

indicators.note: during puts the breathing organ inside the exercise letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
a lung is the organ one breathes with

explanation.surface: A swimmer takes a short rest in a workout before diving in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' looks like a rest; it is an organ that breathes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive or headlong leap into water is the verb's core sense.

clue.text: Strip off and run about round the bay

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters go around the bay word
about tells us the letters of run are moved around

parts.note: a cove is a small bay

explanation.surface: A swimmer undresses and jogs round the bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes UNR from 'run', and 'round' puts it around COVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose or lay bare by taking away what covers it.

clue.text: Concerned with origin of device

parts.note: re means concerning or about, as in business letters
a source is a beginning or origin

explanation.surface: Someone is worried about where a gadget came from.
explanation.definitionFit: A device or expedient is a means or stratagem one can fall back on.

clue.text: Player, a violinist, to take part in course

indicators.note: take part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A musician, a violin player, joins in a music course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests study; it is a dish in a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffed pasta squares are served as one part of a meal.

clue.text: Saint overlooks end of prayer-a bit of a bloomer

indicators.note: in a down clue, overlooks puts the saint above what follows

parts.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: A saint ignores the close of prayers, quite a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' sounds like a mistake; it means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollen-bearing organ is a part of a flower.

clue.text: Crazy impulse to build an engine

parts.note: loco is slang for mad
a motive is a driving impulse

explanation.surface: A wild urge to build a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway engine pulls trains; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: David loses his head, being greedy

indicators.note: his head is the first letter of the name, which is taken off

explanation.surface: A man named David goes mad with greed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses his head' sounds like panic; here it removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager and grasping are close synonyms for keen to have more.

clue.text: Tread on ghastly pest

indicators.note: ghastly suggests a horrible mess, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Squashing a horrible bug underfoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A footfall or pace is the same as a tread.

clue.text: Donor finds American soldier very short

parts.note: a GI is a US soldier

indicators.note: short means the word for very loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A benefactor turns out to be a small US serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is one who makes a gift.

clue.text: It might give NATO harm in the long run

indicators.note: the answer's letters, shuffled, might produce the words that follow, so they are an anagram

explanation.surface: Some policy could damage the alliance eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the long run' reads as 'eventually', but 'the long run' is the definition; the anagram runs from answer to fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A 26-mile road race is the archetypal long-distance run.

clue.text: Stupidly, peer interferes with capitalist system

indicators.note: stupidly means the letters are handled foolishly and so jumbled

explanation.surface: A foolish lord meddles with the market economy.
explanation.definitionFit: A market economy run by private business with little state control.
